# In brief {.unnumbered}

**DF-GLC is coded correctly.** It agrees with an independent solver to rounding error, and its s.d. is exactly
right when the data are as DF-GLC assumes them, with its settings known or fitted, including the search over the
pattern's shape.

**Its limitations:**

1. **Its resolution matches GCM's at 200–800 km**: with noise, 79% of the contrast of 815 km tiles, 66% at 407 km
   and 30% at 204 km.
2. **Unlike GCM, it keeps very broad patterns**: 78% of the contrast of 1630 km tiles, against GCM's 44%. Its
   correlated pattern carries them, as CM's smooth field does over Australia.
3. **Its s.d. is too narrow for sharp edges.** For the checkerboards only 44–75% of cells are within 1 s.d.
4. **Noise-free data do not help it**, because its noise level is held fixed rather than fitted.

# What is checked, and how {#sec-method}

DF-GLC uses DF's model (a level per domain, spread τ about one shared level, and a fractal pattern inside each
domain, starting afresh at its boundary) in the global fit of GCM: the same 22,591 cells and 17,700 coefficients
(degrees 16–133). The pattern's strength s is shared by all domains, and the data are weighted for the noise and for
an error of the ocean model at 16 nT (ADR 0009). The real runs fit s and τ by the evidence on each of a few shapes
(β 2, 2.5, 3 × ℓ 350, 700, 1400 km) and keep the best.

Each shape takes 13–21 minutes to prepare (a decomposition of a 17,700 × 17,700 matrix); after that, a new data set
costs seconds. The tests prepare each shape once and reuse it for every truth. The synthetic data are the truth's
coefficients from the inversion's own cell columns plus noise as DF-GLC models it.

# Correctness checks {#sec-correct}

DF-GLC was checked at one shape (β 2, ℓ 700 km) with the groups layout of the real runs (437 domains), against an
independent solver that builds the covariance block by block and solves the full system without the
decomposition (@fig-df-glc-d1).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Log evidence | Equal to rounding (difference 0) |
| The level v0 | Equal to 3×10⁻¹⁶ SI·km |
| Map, every cell | Equal to 5×10⁻¹³ SI·km |
| s.d., every cell | Equal to 1×10⁻¹³ (relative) |

![DF-GLC against the independent solver, for a truth drawn from DF-GLC's own model (groups
layout).](figures/df_glc_d1_maps.png){#fig-df-glc-d1}

## Uncertainties

Twenty truths were drawn from DF-GLC's own model with the groups layout (level 0.7, τ 0.1, s 0.4 SI·km, β 2, ℓ
700 km, close to the real groups fit) and inverted three ways (@fig-df-glc-spread).

| Settings | Error / s.d., spread (should be 1) | Within 1 s.d. (68%) | Within 2 s.d. (95%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| At the truth | 1.002 | 68.2% | 95.4% |
| s and τ fitted at the true shape | 1.005 | 68.0% | 95.3% |
| s, τ and the shape fitted, as the real runs do | 1.005 | 68.0% | 95.3% |

The search found the true shape in 19 of 20 truths; in the other it chose ℓ 1400 km and put τ at its lower limit,
the same trade-off between patch size and level spread as in DF for Australia. The strength came back at 0.396–0.404
SI·km and τ at 0.063–0.119 (middle 68% of truths). With 17,700 data and three settings, fitting them costs nothing,
unlike DF for Australia, whose s.d. becomes 1.2 times too small with its 43 settings fitted to 849 data.

![DF-GLC's errors in units of its reported s.d., over all cells of 20 truths: settings at the truth, fitted at the
true shape, and fitted with the shape searched.](figures/df_glc_d2_spread.png){#fig-df-glc-spread}

# Limitations {#sec-limits}

## How large and how small a pattern DF-GLC can see

The equal-area checkerboards of the GCM part were inverted with DF-GLC as one domain (one pattern without breaks),
with the shape searched, without noise and with the same noise draw as GCM (@fig-df-glc-shrink-maps,
@fig-df-glc-shrink-contrast).

| Tile size | DF-GLC, no noise | DF-GLC, noise | GCM, noise | Shape chosen (noise) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1630 km | 0.75 | 0.78 | 0.44 | β 3, ℓ 700 km |
| 815 km | 0.79 | 0.79 | 0.77 | β 2.5, ℓ 350 km |
| 407 km | 0.66 | 0.66 | 0.67 | β 2.5, ℓ 350 km |
| 204 km | 0.28 | 0.30 | 0.33 | β 2, ℓ 350 km |

: The recovered contrast, as a fraction of the true contrast. {#tbl-df-glc-shrink}

- **At 200–800 km DF-GLC and GCM recover the same contrast.** The data set the limit, not the method.
- **At 1630 km DF-GLC keeps 78% of the contrast, GCM 44%.** This confirms the explanation in the GCM part: a pattern
  correlated over hundreds of kilometres carries broad features that the data constrain only weakly below degree 16;
  GCM's independent cells cannot.
- **Its s.d. is too narrow for sharp edges**: 44–75% of cells within 1 s.d. A smooth pattern cannot draw square
  edges, and its s.d. does not allow for that, as for DF with the wrong domains in Australia.
- **Noise-free data do not help.** DF-GLC holds the noise at its measured level (the real runs' `noise = "fixed"`),
  so it treats exact data as noisy; GCM fits the noise level and recovers 68–97% without noise.
- **The shape grid limits the smallest tiles.** For tiles of 815 km and less the best ℓ was the smallest on the grid
  (350 km). The real run then tries 175 km too; this test did not, so DF-GLC may do slightly better at 204–407 km than
  shown.

![Checkerboards of equal-area tiles of 1630, 815, 407 and 204 km (rows): the truth, then DF-GLC (one domain) without
and with noise, with the shape it chose.](figures/df_glc_shrink_maps.png){#fig-df-glc-shrink-maps}

![The recovered contrast against the tile size, DF-GLC and GCM on the same truths and the same
noise.](figures/df_glc_shrink_contrast.png){#fig-df-glc-shrink-contrast}

# What this means for real DF-GLC maps {#sec-meaning}

- **The s.d. is right when the model is right**, but too narrow where VIS changes sharply inside a domain.
- **Read features of about 400 km and larger**; broad features are better kept than in GCM.
- **Small features (about 200 km) lose two-thirds of their contrast**, as in every method with these data.

# Rerunning {#sec-rerun}

The code is `benchmarks/verification/df_glc_checks.py` (tests `d1`, `d2`, `d3`), with the maps drawn by
`docs/verification/make_df_glc_figures.py`; the commands are at the top of this document's source. The tests use the
configuration `inversions/df_glc_lcs1_16-133.toml`, run in one process (20–40 GB of memory), keep the shape
decompositions in `benchmarks/verification/cache/df_glc` (so a stopped run resumes), and write their results to
`benchmarks/verification/results/df_glc_*`.
